claims.text: A predictive method incorporating point defects and 1 wt.% oxygen through statistical or machine-learning algorithms will predict the thermal conductivity of bulk HfNbTaTiZr more accurately than conventional analytical models.
The bulk HfNbTaTiZr specimen has an inherent defect landscape and approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
Defect variations and oxygen impurities influence thermal transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed model will be trained on data spanning defect variations, oxygen effects, and diverse temperatures.
The prediction is intended to cover the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K temperature regimes.
Point defects and oxygen-related impurity sites alter phonon scattering and lattice dynamics.
Conventional analytical approaches assume perfect, defect-free crystals.
Including oxygen impurities and defect-induced phonon scattering enables a more realistic simulation of phonon transport.
Capturing temperature-dependent anomalies caused by non-idealities will reduce thermal-conductivity prediction error.
The proposed model will closely match measured thermal conductivity throughout both specified temperature regimes.
The proposed model will have significantly lower prediction error than existing analytical models.
The largest improvement will occur near the boundaries of the two temperature regimes because defect scattering has a particularly strong influence there.
Perfect-lattice analytical predictions tend to deviate from experiment because they omit the defect landscape and oxygen content.
The proposed approach is limited primarily to bulk HfNbTaTiZr specimens with defect profiles similar to the training specimens and approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
Accuracy outside 0–200 K and 300–1200 K, or for substantially different defect or impurity concentrations, is unverified.
The magnitude of improvement depends on the quality and representativeness of the training data.
Prior quantitative data on defect-induced thermal-conductance changes in these high-entropy alloys are limited.
The hypothesis is falsified if the proposed approach fails to reduce RMSE by at least 20% relative to the conventional model over both temperature regimes.
